Valley-biased gamma uses (1-h01)^(1/g) — mathematically unusual height inversion; correct for Brucks-style valley-bias but undocumented. Python loop over L channels acceptable (L typically 5). Missing: no vectorized numpy path for larger channel counts.
Checks cliff_mask coverage vs total area with configurable threshold. Returns ValidationIssue list. Clean contract.

Uses aspect ratio of cliff bounding box as proxy for silhouette elongation. Bounding-box aspect ratio is a weak proxy — L-shaped cliffs and branching cliffs would both fail or pass incorrectly. A connected-component-per-cluster elongation check would be more accurate.
Clean frozen dataclass. All required fields present. Missing: no declared PBR color space (sRGB vs linear) on base_color, which creates ambiguity downstream for compositors.

Reconstructs normal Z from XY via sqrt(1 - x^2 - y^2). Clamps to [0, 1] for safety. Correct and vectorized.

Implements Brucks-style height-based weight blending with contrast parameter. Softmax normalization after height-blend is correct. Well-commented. Missing: no test for degenerate case where all weights are zero after blending.

Sigmoid altitude curve modulated by slope exposure. Configurable via climate_params dict. Temperature lapse rate not modeled (would need elevation_m, not normalized height). Functional for game purposes.

Bilinear sampling of a macro color array at fractional coordinates. Manual bilinear interpolation is correct but duplicates the pattern in terrain_math and terrain_saliency. Should call a shared utility.
Reads road_sdf channel and applies smoothstep blend toward road material. Gracefully skips when channel absent. Clean.

Inconsistent quality within the same function.

Calls slope_radians, converts to degrees. Clean wrapper.

Critical performance flaw: the scipy fast path (EDT) is correct O(N), but the Python chamfer fallback has TWO nested O(H*W) loops per direction pass. For 2049x2049 tiles this is 16.8M iterations per forward/backward pass in pure Python — will take minutes and block the pipeline. The two-pass Borgefors 3-4-5 algorithm is correct but must be in numpy/C, not Python loops. AAA pipelines would never ship a fallback this slow.

Critical PBR flaw: normalizes integer textures by dtype.max but does NOT apply sRGB gamma linearization. Albedo textures are stored in sRGB (gamma ~2.2) and must be linearized before PBR mixing. Without linearization, albedo blending happens in perceptually-encoded space, producing darker-than-correct results at blend midpoints. This is the #1 PBR pipeline mistake. Normal, roughness, AO, displacement channels do NOT need linearization (they are stored in linear space already) — but albedo does. Needs TextureType-aware gamma decode.
Tag-based biome matching with fallback to True when no tags present. Permissive but functional.

Orchestrates asset ingestion. Reads all texture types, writes to appropriate stack channels. terrain_ao and terrain_displacement ARE written correctly. AO: correctly treated as linear (no gamma needed). Displacement: correctly linear. Inherits sRGB issue from _load_texture_as_float for albedo.
Bilinear sampling with edge-safe clamping. Python channel loop for 3D tensors (C <= 3, acceptable for asset ingest, not tight inner loop).

Applies Quixel textures to splatmap layer via weight mask. Inherits sRGB issue. Missing: no mip-level selection — large tile sizes will sample the same full-res texture regardless of display distance.

SHA-256-based deterministic RNG factory using list-form default_rng (correct for parallel seeding per NumPy docs). The hashing scheme produces uint32 seeds from str(key) — correct but truncates to 4 bytes out of 32 (loses entropy). Critical gap: FUTURE USE comment reveals this is only called from tests, not from production passes. Ad-hoc np.random.RandomState calls elsewhere in the codebase are not yet migrated (BUG-48/49/81/91/92/96 open). The tool exists but isn't enforced — so the seeding scheme is half-implemented.
Convenience wrapper using world_origin * 1000 for integer conversion. Also FUTURE USE only. Same migration gap as make_rng.
World-to-grid conversion with rounding and clamping. Correct. Duplicates the function in terrain_math but harmless duplication within the file's pure-numpy scope.
Edge-safe bilinear height sampling. Correctly clamps r0/c0 to [0, rows-2] before r0+1 access. Well-handled degenerate 1-row/col case.

Casts azimuthal rays from each vantage, detects sky-terrain horizon transitions. Vectorized ray sampling (ray_count x n_samples at once). scipy map_coordinates for sub-pixel sampling when available, manual bilinear fallback. Silhouette scoring via arctan2 + transition bonus is design-correct. This matches the documented Witcher 3 / Horizon ZD composition approach.

Desire-line gradient-following height delta. Positive features get gradient-aligned ridge emphasis; negative features get erosion channel via flow proxy. Gaussian envelope blending. More sophisticated than radial Gaussian. Not a full hydrological simulation but appropriate for game authoring. Vectorized numpy throughout.

Projects silhouette scores onto grid via arctan2 ray binning. Inverse-square falloff. FOV forward-weighting. No per-cell Python loop (vectorized via arctan2 grid computation). Not true DDA (the function name claims DDA but uses angle binning) — naming is misleading but result is functionally correct for accumulation purposes.

8-factor UE5-style saliency scoring: height visibility, water proximity (EDT), slope shelter (Laplacian), ridge prominence (TPI), convexity (prominence), sky exposure, vegetation-break potential, tactical sight-line. All factors normalized [0,1] and blended 1/8 each. Factors have real AAA composition grounding. scipy paths for all computationally intensive operations. Falls back to numpy approximations without scipy. High-quality implementation.

Reads vantages from intent, computes silhouettes, applies 8-factor scoring. Blends 50/50 with existing saliency_macro (tactical_influence up to 0.5, scales with vantage count). Returns rich metrics. Well-designed pass contract. Correctly marks idempotent=False (result depends on vantage state).
Validates saliency_macro has meaningful variance after refinement. Checks std >= 0.02 and mean in [0.05, 0.95]. Returns soft ValidationIssues. Non-blocking gate appropriate for a diagnostic check.
QualityGate instance wrapping _saliency_quality_gate. blocking=False (soft). Clean.

Returns 0-1 salience proxy from tier or weight field. tier_map (primary=1.0, secondary=0.6, tertiary=0.3, ambient=0.1) is design-grounded.
Returns nearest-neighbour distances via cKDTree (fast) or N² fallback. Correct.

Simplified Ripley K(r) without edge correction. Returns L(r) = sqrt(K/pi) - r. Correctly mirrors spatial statistics approach for density validation. Edge correction omission is appropriate for terrain-scale analysis (boundary effects are << tile size).

Spearman rank correlation via 8-bin histogram. The argsort(argsort()) double-ranking is correct but could be simplified with scipy.stats.spearmanr. Results with only 8 bins can be granular. Functional but imprecise for sparse point sets.

Comprehensive rhythm analysis: NN statistics, Ripley K proxy, density gradients. 50k point cap for performance. Returns well-documented metrics dict. AAA target of ~0.6 rhythm (CV ~0.4) is design-grounded (matches Guerrilla/Naughty Dog QA thresholds cited in code).

Two-path strategy: clustered → prune lowest-salience duplicates; overdispersed/in-range → Lloyd relaxation. Respects HeroFeatureSpec frozen status (never moves or removes anchored features). Convergence check prevents infinite loops. Rebuilds output types correctly. Well-designed.

Groups by feature type, runs analyze_feature_rhythm per type, emits typed ValidationIssues. Six distinct checks (too_random, too_regular, clustered, overdispersed, density_gradient, min_spacing_violated). Hard min_spacing violations correctly categorized as hard severity. High-quality validation.

Requires roughness_breakup to enforce DAG ordering. Clean registration.

Fully vectorized bilinear heightmap sampling. Feathering via smoothstep. Four blend modes (add/replace/max/min) all vectorized. Correct UV coordinate mapping. No Python loops over vertices. High-quality.
8-connected (Moore neighbourhood) adjacency from bmesh. Includes edge-sharing + face-diagonal neighbours. Sorted for determinism. Matches ZBrush/Houdini topology-smooth kernel definition.

World→local transform for brush center via matrix_world.inverted(). XY-averaged scale for radius conversion. Dispatches to all 5 sculpt modes. Atomic displacement application with bounds clamping. Computes slope angle in degrees from face normal. Correct arccos of nz component. Handles zero-length normal.

5-factor face classification: slope, water level, curvature modulation (±4 degrees). Water edge takes priority. Curvature shift is well-motivated (concave faces accumulate soil, convex faces express bare rock). Missing: no hysteresis — faces near boundaries can flip classification on tiny changes.

5-factor pure-logic classification: slope, altitude band (5 tiers: water/treeline/snowline/standard/cliff), rock hardness (shifts thresholds ±10-15°), wetness (aspect-corrected), aspect (north/south solar exposure ±0.15 moisture bias). Boundary dithering via face index parity. Python loop over faces — not ideal for large mesh counts but pure-logic function not on hot path. Well-grounded in World Creator 2 / GeoGlyph conventions.

4-channel splatmap blending (RGBA = grass/rock/dirt/special). Three axes: slope drives rock/grass, altitude drives special (snow/water), wetness drives dirt/grass. Correct sRGB linearization for blending with re-encoding at output. Python loop over vertices — would be slow on AAA meshes (500k+ vertices). Should be vectorized with numpy or moved to a pass function. Logic quality is good.
